players.product: 800G/1.6T PAM4 ICs, 200G/lane photodetectors, TIAs/drivers, CW lasers (developing) for optical modules

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 revenue was $342.2 million, up 18.4% sequentially and 35.8% year over year, with all three end markets growing. Adjusted gross profit was $204.2 million or 59.7% of revenue, a 120 basis point sequential improvement. Adjusted operating income was a record $107.7 million, up 33.9% sequentially and 69.6% year over year, giving a 31.5% adjusted operating margin versus 25.2% a year earlier. Adjusted operating expenses were $96.5 million (R&D $65.3 million, SG&A $31.2 million). Adjusted net income rose 30.2% to $109.8 million and adjusted EPS was $1.40 on 78.4 million diluted shares, versus $1.09 in fiscal Q2. The adjusted tax rate was 3%, expected to rise toward mid-single digits through fiscal 2027 as profitability increases.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $342.2M (+18.4% QoQ, +35.8% YoY); adjusted gross margin 59.7%; adjusted operating margin 31.5%; adjusted EPS $1.40

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q4 2026 guidance (quarter ending October 2, 2026): revenue of $415-425 million, adjusted gross margin of 60-61%, and adjusted EPS of $1.97-2.03 on 78.9 million fully diluted shares, with adjusted operating margin expected at approximately 37%. By segment MACOM expects approximately 35% sequential growth in Data Center, approximately 20% in Industrial and Defense, and low single-digit growth in Telecom. Management framed a fiscal 2027 BASE CASE by annualising the Q4 midpoint: mid-20s company growth (27-28%) with DATA CENTER TRENDING TO 50% year-over-year growth. Gross margin should keep improving sequentially but at a more measured 25-50 basis points per quarter, and the target for next year is to BREACH A 40% OPERATING MARGIN.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 guide $415M-$425M, adjusted GM 60-61%, EPS $1.97-$2.03, ~37% operating margin; FY2027 base case ~27-28% company growth with Data Center ~50%

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 book-to-bill was a RECORD 1.6:1 - up from 1.3 in Q1 and 1.5 in Q2 - producing MACOM's highest quarterly bookings ever and a record backlog, with all three end markets posting exceptional bookings and notable outperformance in Data Center. Orders booked and shipped within the quarter (turns business) were only 11% of total revenue, so visibility is strong. Management said the book-to-bill trend suggests fiscal 2027 starts in a very strong position. Customer concentration keeps falling: two years ago MACOM had roughly eight customers above $10 million of revenue, today over 20 are above $10 million with a few in the $50-100 million range, and the year-to-date top 10 end customers are still less than 40% of total revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Record book-to-bill 1.6:1 (Q1 1.3, Q2 1.5); highest quarterly bookings ever; turns business 11% of revenue; top 10 customers <40% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Data Center revenue was a record $137.6 million, up approximately 40% sequentially, driven by 800G and 1.6T PAM4 demand. The segment grew 35% in 2024 and 48% in 2025 and is trending toward about 74% THIS YEAR. The primary driver from fiscal 2025 to 2026 is 200-gig PAM4 products in pluggable optical modules; ZR and ZR-light are growing over 100% year over year; 100-gig-per-lane single mode and multimode are posting high double-digit growth; and legacy 25-gig-per-lane products for 100G FR and LR4 are also growing strongly. Book-to-bill within Data Center is driven primarily by 1.6T and 800G platforms. MACOM is sampling its latest generation 200G and 400G PER LANE TIAs and drivers. A structural tailwind: hyperscalers are moving from PASSIVE COPPER TO FIBER in scale-up applications, which is pure SAM expansion for MACOM because it does not promote passive copper solutions.
quarterly_data.figure: Data Center revenue $137.6M (+~40% QoQ, record); segment growth 35% in 2024, 48% in 2025, ~74% trending this year

quarterly_data.signal: NPO and XPO positioning: MACOM has BETWEEN 10 AND 20 ACTIVE NPO DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS across various customers and use cases, and expects some of that revenue to kick in IN 2028, with NPO starting to grow significantly from 2028. Critically, MACOM says it will NOT build or supply optical engines - in Data Center it is a chip supplier, not a multichip assembly or module supplier. It describes the architectural evolution as pluggable transceivers with DSPs, to LPO platforms that remove the DSP, morphing into smaller package-less NPO platforms; those architectures still need drivers and TIAs, but with much higher density - smaller parts, more channels, lower power, and varied form factors using wire bonds, bumped devices or flip chip, plus through-silicon-via options. Because these solutions are specific to the architectures hyperscalers are driving, the design wins come directly to MACOM. Related applications include LPO and LRO on single mode or multimode.
quarterly_data.figure: 10-20 active NPO development projects; NPO revenue expected to begin in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Indium phosphide is the key medium-term lever. 200-GIG PHOTODETECTORS are ramping in volume production and becoming a meaningful contributor to Data Center growth; 400-gig photodetectors are in the hands of perhaps a dozen customers with very positive feedback. The 75-MILLIWATT CW LASER qualification continues: MACOM is well into HTOL testing (typically 5,000 hours) with data described as exceptional, is gaining confidence but cannot yet declare success, and is developing plans for a POTENTIAL START TO PRODUCTION IN LATE CALENDAR 2027, scoping modest capex and fab space for a rapid high-volume ramp for a few strategic customers. CEO Steve Daly called bringing a CW laser into production in 2028 'a watershed moment' that could be a very large revenue contributor. Separately, demand for MACOM's 25G DFB lasers (100G QSFP, CWDM4, LR4) is rising with urgency because of a GENERAL SUPPLY SHORTAGE OF INDIUM PHOSPHIDE DFB LASERS. MACOM expects to gain meaningful indium phosphide market share over the next three years; its Ann Arbor, Michigan facility has built photodiodes for over a decade and grows its own epitaxy by MBE.
quarterly_data.figure: 200G PDs ramping in volume; 400G PDs at ~a dozen customers; 75mW CW laser potential production start late calendar 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and lead times: utilisation at the RTP, North Carolina and Lowell, Massachusetts fabs continues to increase even as capacity is added, and utilisation rates are now IMPACTING LEAD TIMES - MACOM is quoting LONGER LEAD TIMES for internally manufactured products. New capacity is being added across operations through the remainder of fiscal 2026 and into fiscal 2027, and management notes new-capacity capex is typically installed and online in less than one year per project. Fiscal 2026 capex is estimated at $60-65 million (versus $22.4 million in fiscal 2024 and $42.6 million in fiscal 2025), with fiscal 2027 capex expected to be similar at roughly $60 million including infrastructure to support a laser ramp. The Massachusetts fab mix is now a combination of Telecom, Defense and Data Center as indium phosphide ramps.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 capex $60M-$65M, FY2027 similar ~$60M; longer lead times being quoted on internally manufactured products

quarterly_data.signal: On the proposed U.S. ban on Chinese transceiver module makers, CEO Steve Daly said MACOM's Data Center growth is driven by U.S. hyperscalers plus U.S. enterprise and compute OEMs, and that those end users are typically directly involved in selecting chips for their hardware. If hyperscalers have to shift share between transceiver companies because of new regulations, 'we would expect to follow that business to those other manufacturers' - a customer mix shift rather than a demand loss, since MACOM has relationships with most transceiver companies in the industry. MACOM has NO MANUFACTURING IN CHINA, only about 85 employees there in application sales and logistics supporting Scandinavian telecom design centres and the optical industry, and the vast majority of what it sells into China is exported back out inside systems typically headed to the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: No manufacturing in China; ~85 employees there in sales/logistics

quarterly_data.signal: MACOM published its 2026-2030 Growth Strategy Plan to the Board in mid-July and reset its served addressable market to approximately $15 BILLION IN 2027 - roughly $6 billion Industrial and Defense, $6 billion Data Center and about $3 billion Telecom - up about 20% to 30% from 2026. Named accelerators for the next three to five years: more 200-gig-per-lane PAM4 products, added indium phosphide capacity, new scale-up, scale-out and scale-across programs, NPO growing significantly from 2028, coherent light opportunities, PCIe 6, and linear equalizers. On equalizers specifically, MACOM sees opportunity in both active copper cables and on-board (PCB) use, and said ONE LARGE HYPERSCALER is looking to deploy that type of cable solution at large volumes, where MACOM would expect to participate when it moves to production. R&D spending has roughly doubled in three years, from about $132 million in 2023 to almost $250 million this year.
quarterly_data.figure: 2027 SAM ~$15B (I&D ~$6B, Data Center ~$6B, Telecom ~$3B), up 20-30% vs 2026; R&D ~$250M this year vs ~$132M in 2023

quarterly_data.signal: Telecom revenue was $71.3 million, up 2% sequentially, and is forecast to grow double digits this year with similar or better performance expected next year. LEO satellite broadband and direct-to-device remain robust: MACOM serves four or five major LEO customers, has two or three major LEO programs starting production at the end of this calendar year and the beginning of next, and this quarter WAS SELECTED TO SUPPORT A NEXT-GENERATION SATELLITE OPTICAL COMMUNICATION PLATFORM at a large satellite OEM - a win management expects to drive growth for two to three years, won because all the critical ICs for the system could be sourced from MACOM. The commercial RF power team traditionally aimed at 5G base stations is now also targeting LEO, since 5G technology applies directly to LEO D2D. MACOM demonstrated linearisation of a high-power V-band TWT and a complete W-band (~75 GHz) transmit/receive signal chain at IMS. Within Telecom, 5G is still the largest piece with two competitors having exited in the last three to four years; cable infrastructure is growing around 40% year over year and metro long-haul over 50% this year.
quarterly_data.figure: Telecom $71.3M (+2% QoQ); cable infrastructure ~+40% YoY; metro long-haul >50% growth; selected for a next-generation satellite optical communication platform

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet and cash flow: cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $663 million at July 3, 2026, against $340.5 million of convertible notes maturing in December 2029, leaving a net cash position of approximately $322.5 million. Fiscal Q3 cash flow from operations was approximately $80 million with Q4 expected in excess of $100 million. Capital expenditures were $20.8 million in the quarter. Accounts receivable rose $19.5 million to $179.1 million with DSO improving to 48 days from 50; inventories rose to $281.5 million from $252.2 million to support demand, with turns up 0.1x to 2x. Input costs - labour, electricity, utilities and raw materials - are rising, and while MACOM passes cost on where it can, it has still expanded gross margin.
quarterly_data.figure: $663M cash and short-term investments; net cash ~$322.5M; Q3 OCF ~$80M, Q4 expected >$100M; Q3 capex $20.8M

players.product: AI data center power supply products (SiC-based)

quarterly_data.signal: Industrial and Defense revenue was a record $133.4 million, up 11% sequentially. The Defense business grew 19% last year and is expected to grow approximately 25% this year across radar, missile and missile defense, drone and drone-defense, communications and wideband electronic warfare systems. At the International Microwave Symposium in June MACOM showcased an X-band front-end module built from its GaN ICs in a highly integrated multichip module, delivering 16 WATTS of transmit power and OVER 40% power added efficiency in a footprint suited to compact high-volume radar. MACOM also received INCREMENTAL FUNDING FROM THE AIR FORCE RESEARCH LABS to support MILLIMETER WAVE GaN-ON-SILICON CARBIDE production maturation. Industrial submarkets - test and measurement, medical, automotive and general multi-market - are also improving, with test and measurement demand driven partly by AI-related engineering and production facilitation, and the small automotive business expected to double its revenue this year.
quarterly_data.figure: I&D revenue $133.4M (+11% QoQ, record); defense +19% last year, ~25% expected this year; X-band GaN module at 16W and >40% PAE

quarterly_data.signal: Compound semiconductor manufacturing build-out. In Q3 MACOM began installing a new G10 EPITAXIAL REACTOR at the MACOM European Semiconductor Center (MESC) in France to support future growth and technology development for European commercial and defense markets. MESC completed conversion of one production line FROM 3-INCH TO 6-INCH this year with two more process sets to convert in the next four to six months - a conversion that improves quality, reduces cost and DOUBLES CAPACITY, and which many defense contractors have been waiting for. MACOM expects to receive one of the largest orders in MESC's history from a U.K. defense company working on airborne defense systems within a month or two, and expects European defense revenue to start growing materially around 2028. The France site was acquired as a 'fixer-upper' for about EUR 38 million against roughly EUR 25 million of land value and approximately $100 million of capital equipment.
quarterly_data.figure: MESC 3-inch to 6-inch conversion doubles capacity; European defense revenue to grow materially around 2028; site acquired for ~EUR 38M

quarterly_data.signal: Two U.S. manufacturing notes. First, when WOLFSPEED SHUT DOWN ITS DURHAM FAB, MACOM acquired equipment at attractive prices and put it into service, and has been expanding capacity in Lowell. Second, on the CHIPS Office: a January 2025 plan contemplated $345 MILLION of total investment over five years across the North Carolina and Massachusetts fabs, roughly half expected to be funded by the U.S. government and half by MACOM. Because that plan was written in 2024, MACOM has updated and RESUBMITTED the project plan to reflect changed capabilities and actions already taken, and negotiations on the terms of any definitive agreement continue.
quarterly_data.figure: CHIPS plan: $345M total investment over five years across North Carolina and Massachusetts fabs, roughly half government funded
